slot.brief: Series LCR circuit with given component values and source frequency; compute the phase angle between current and voltage and state whether the circuit is inductive or capacitive.

stem: In a series $LCR$ circuit, $R = 100\ \Omega$, $L = 0.2\text{ H}$, and $C = 10\ \mu\text{F}$ are connected to an AC source of angular frequency $\omega = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. The phase angle between the voltage and the current, and the nature of the circuit are:

verdicts.working: X_L = ωL = 1000×0.2 = 200 Ω; X_C = 1/(ωC) = 1/(1000×10⁻⁵) = 100 Ω. Net reactance X_L − X_C = +100 Ω (inductive). tan φ = 100/R = 100/100 = 1 ⇒ φ = 45°, voltage leads current (inductive).

working:
1. Calculate inductive reactance:
$$X_L = \omega L = 1000 \times 0.2 = 200\ \Omega$$

2. Calculate capacitive reactance:
$$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{1000 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1}{10^{-2}} = 100\ \Omega$$

3. Determine the nature of the circuit:
Since $X_L > X_C$ ($200\ \Omega > 100\ \Omega$), inductive reactance dominates, so the circuit is inductive (voltage leads current).

4. Calculate the phase angle $\phi$:
$$\tan\phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R} = \dfrac{200 - 100}{100} = \dfrac{100}{100} = 1$$
$$\implies \phi = 45^\circ$$

Thus, the phase angle is $45^\circ$ and the circuit is inductive.

Independent check: X_L = ωL = 1000×0.2 = 200 Ω; X_C = 1/(ωC) = 1/(1000×10⁻⁵) = 100 Ω. Net reactance X_L − X_C = +100 Ω (inductive). tan φ = 100/R = 100/100 = 1 ⇒ φ = 45°, voltage leads current (inductive).

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A: Finds the correct angle ($45^\circ$) but confuses which reactance dominates, mistakenly labeling the circuit capacitive.
Option C: Obtains impedance by simple scalar addition $Z = R + (X_L - X_C) = 200\ \Omega$, finds $\cos\phi = R/Z = 1/2 \implies \phi = 60^\circ$, and also mislabels the circuit as capacitive.
Option D: Uses scalar addition of resistance and reactance ($Z = R + X_L - X_C = 200\ \Omega$) instead of phasor addition, giving $\cos\phi = R/Z = 1/2 \implies \phi = 60^\circ$.
